note: HSK 5 reading rounds in the 新版HSK (2025-12) format, Mainland edition: 第一部分 完形填空 ×10 (passages with numbered blanks, four options each), 第二部分 ×10 (46–50 段落填句 with six sentences — a guess, the 样题 shows only 51–55; 51–55 five paragraphs in order), 第三部分 长文阅读 ×15 (texts with 3–4 questions); 4 options, pinyin hidden; the mock exam is 35 minutes. Original texts, words within HSK 1–5. Drafted 2026-10-30 in tools/.mockups/hsk5_rd.py.

items.text: 随着生活水平的提高，越来越多的人开始（　）健康饮食。不少人每天都会计算自己吃了多少东西，（　）有的人还会专门请人帮自己安排一日三餐。专家指出，健康饮食最重要的是（　），而不是简单地少吃。

tr.en: As living standards rise, more and more people pay attention to eating healthily. Many count how much they eat every day, and some even hire someone to plan their three meals. Experts point out that the key to healthy eating is all-round nutrition, not simply eating less.

questions.zh: 「重視」健康飲食，是認為它重要、關心它。
questions.en: 重视 (attach importance to) healthy eating.

questions.zh: 前面說計算吃多少，後面說更進一步的「請人安排三餐」，用「甚至」。
questions.en: 甚至 (even) introduces a further step.

questions.zh: 和「簡單地少吃」相對的是吃得「營養全面」。
questions.en: The opposite of just eating less is all-round nutrition.

items.text: 小王大学毕业后，没有像其他同学一样留在大城市，而是（　）回到了家乡。他用自己学到的知识，帮村里的人在网上卖水果。一开始，很多人对他的做法（　），认为在网上卖东西不可靠。（　），村里的水果不但卖到了全国各地，价格也比以前高了不少，大家这才相信了他。

tr.en: After graduating, Xiao Wang didn't stay in a big city like his classmates but chose to go back to his home village. With what he had learnt, he helped the villagers sell fruit online. At first many doubted his approach, thinking selling online was unreliable. Unexpectedly, a year later the village fruit was selling all over the country at much better prices, and only then did they believe in him.

questions.zh: 沒有留在大城市，而是「選擇」回家鄉。
questions.en: 选择 (choose) to go home.

questions.zh: 後面說「認為在網上賣東西不可靠」，所以是懷疑。
questions.en: They thought it unreliable: they doubted it.

questions.zh: 後面是出乎大家意料的好結果，用「沒想到一年以後」。
questions.en: An unexpected good result: "unexpectedly, a year later".

items.text: 很多人都有这样的经历：（　）去超市只想买一瓶水，结果却推着满满一车东西出来。其实，这和超市的（　）有很大关系。超市一般会把面包、牛奶这些每天都要买的东西放在最里面，顾客要走过整个超市才能拿到。在这个过程中，人们很容易被其他商品（　），结果就买了很多计划外的东西。所以，去超市以前最好先把要买的东西写下来，（　）。

tr.en: Many people know this: you go to the supermarket meaning to buy just a bottle of water and come out pushing a full trolley. This has a lot to do with how supermarkets are designed. They usually put everyday items like bread and milk at the very back, so customers must walk through the whole shop to reach them. On the way, people are easily attracted by other goods and end up buying many unplanned things. So before going, it's best to write down what you need and buy only that.

questions.zh: 「本來……結果卻……」：原來的打算和結果不一樣。
questions.en: 本来… 结果却…: the plan versus what happened.

questions.zh: 後面說東西放在哪兒，是超市的「設計」。
questions.en: Where goods are placed: the design.

questions.zh: 被其他商品「吸引」，所以買了計劃外的東西。
questions.en: 吸引 (attract): drawn to other goods.

questions.zh: 把要買的東西寫下來，是為了只買需要的東西。
questions.en: The point of writing it down: buy only that.

items.text: 我的爷爷做了一生的家具。（　）。小时候，我最喜欢待在他的工作间里，看他把普通的木头变成漂亮的桌子和椅子。爷爷常说，做家具和做人一样，（　）。有一次，一位客人急着要一张桌子，希望爷爷三天就做好。（　），因为木头还没有完全干，做出来的桌子用不了多久就会变弯。客人虽然有点儿不高兴，（　）。后来，那张桌子他们家用了二十多年，还跟新的一样。（　），也给我上了重要的一课。

tr.en: My grandfather made furniture all his life. His furniture was well known in our area. As a child I loved staying in his workshop, watching him turn ordinary wood into beautiful tables and chairs. He often said making furniture is like being a person: you mustn't hurry, and still less be careless. Once a customer wanted a table urgently, in three days. But Grandpa said it would take at least a week, because the wood wasn't fully dry and a table made from it would soon bend. The customer was a little unhappy but in the end agreed to wait. That table was used in their home for over twenty years and still looked new. This deeply moved the customer, and taught me an important lesson too.

bank: 不能着急，更不能粗心
但最后还是同意多等几天
所以他从来不收学生
他做的家具在我们那儿很有名
这件事让客人非常感动
爷爷却说至少要一个星期

questions.zh: 先介紹爺爺：他做的傢俱很有名。
questions.en: First, Grandpa's furniture was well known.

questions.zh: 「做傢俱和做人一樣」，接著說道理：不能著急，不能粗心。
questions.en: Like being a person: no hurry, no carelessness.

questions.zh: 客人要三天做好，爺爺「卻」說至少要一個星期，後面說原因。
questions.en: The customer wants three days; Grandpa says a week.

questions.zh: 「雖然有點兒不高興，但最後還是同意多等幾天」。
questions.en: 虽然… 但…: unhappy, but agreed to wait.

questions.zh: 桌子用了二十多年，讓客人很感動。C（不收學生）是多出來的。
questions.en: The table lasted twenty years: the customer was moved. C is the spare.

bank: 第二天早上，小明按时到了学校门口，却发现同学们都已经坐上车了。原来，老师把出发时间提前了半个小时，而他因为没看手机，错过了通知。
学校通知，星期六组织学生去郊区参观，早上八点在学校门口集合。小明很兴奋，前一天晚上早早地就睡了。
从那以后，小明养成了每天晚上看一下班级通知的习惯，再也没有因为这样的事情迟到过。
老师看到他着急的样子，安慰他说没关系，让他赶快上车。可是小明心里很不好意思，因为全车人为了等他，晚出发了十分钟。
回家以后，小明把这件事告诉了妈妈。妈妈说，错过通知不只是别人的问题，自己也要养成及时了解信息的习惯。

tr.en: The school announced a trip to the countryside on Saturday, meeting at the school gate at eight. Xiao Ming was excited and went to bed early the night before. Next morning he arrived on time, only to find his classmates already on the coach: the teacher had moved the departure half an hour earlier, and he had missed the message because he hadn't checked his phone. Seeing how anxious he was, the teacher comforted him and told him to get on quickly, but Xiao Ming felt embarrassed, because everyone had left ten minutes late waiting for him. At home he told his mother, who said missing a notice isn't only other people's fault — you must also get into the habit of keeping informed. From then on he checked the class notices every evening and was never late like that again.

questions.zh: 故事從學校的通知開始：星期六去參觀。
questions.en: It starts with the school's notice.

questions.zh: 「第二天早上」，小明到了學校，發現大家已經上車了。
questions.en: "Next morning": he finds everyone on the coach.

questions.zh: 接著是老師安慰他，大家等了他十分鐘。
questions.en: Then the teacher comforts him.

questions.zh: 「回家以後」，媽媽告訴他要及時瞭解信息。
questions.en: "At home", his mother's advice.

questions.zh: 「從那以後」，他養成了新習慣，是故事的結尾。
questions.en: "From then on": the new habit ends the story.

items.text:
在中国，很多人都有午睡的习惯。吃完午饭后，不少人会在办公桌上睡二三十分钟，学校里的孩子们也会午睡。那么，午睡到底有没有好处呢？
研究表明，适当的午睡可以让大脑得到休息，提高下午的工作效率。特别是晚上睡眠不足的人，中午小睡一会儿，能帮助他们恢复精力。
不过，午睡并不是越长越好。专家建议，午睡的时间最好控制在半个小时以内。如果睡得太久，人会进入深度睡眠，醒来以后反而会觉得头很重、没精神，甚至还会影响晚上的睡眠。
另外，午睡的姿势也很重要。很多人习惯在桌子上睡，这样手和眼睛容易被压着，醒来后手不舒服，看东西也不清楚。条件允许的话，最好能躺下来休息。

tr.en: In China many people nap after lunch: many sleep twenty or thirty minutes at their desks, and schoolchildren nap too. So is a nap good for you? Research shows a moderate nap rests the brain and raises afternoon efficiency; for those short of sleep at night, a short midday sleep helps restore energy. But longer isn't better: experts suggest keeping it under half an hour. Sleep too long and you enter deep sleep, waking heavy-headed and listless, which may even affect your night's sleep. Posture matters too: sleeping on a desk presses on the hands and eyes, leaving the hands uncomfortable and vision unclear. If possible, lie down.

questions.q: 根据第二段，适当的午睡可以：
questions.zh: 「可以讓大腦得到休息，提高下午的工作效率」。
questions.en: "It raises afternoon efficiency."

questions.zh: 「最好控制在半個小時以內」。
questions.en: "Under half an hour."

questions.zh: 「醒來以後反而會覺得頭很重、沒精神」。
questions.en: "You wake dizzy and listless."

questions.q: 关于午睡的姿势，可以知道：
questions.zh: 「條件允許的話，最好能躺下來休息」。
questions.en: "Lie down if you can."

items.text:
李强是一名快递员，每天要送一百多个包裹。他负责的地区住着很多外国人。刚开始，因为语言不通，他常常闹笑话。有一次，一位外国客人想请他帮忙寄东西，两个人比划了半天，也没弄明白对方的意思。
从那以后，李强下定决心学英语。他买了几本英语书，利用送快递时有空的时间背单词，晚上回家再看英语视频。两年过去了，他已经能用英语和外国客人流利地交流了。现在，附近的外国人都喜欢找他寄东西，他的收入也比以前提高了不少。

tr.en: Li Qiang is a courier who delivers over a hundred parcels a day. Many foreigners live in his area. At first, not sharing a language, he often made a fool of himself; once a foreign customer wanted him to send something, and they gestured for ages without understanding each other. After that he resolved to learn English: he bought some books, learnt words in his spare moments between deliveries and watched English videos at night. Two years on he can talk fluently with foreign customers. Now the foreigners nearby like to send things through him, and his income has risen quite a bit.

questions.q: 刚开始，李强为什么常常闹笑话？
questions.zh: 「因為語言不通，他常常鬧笑話」。
questions.en: "Because they had no common language."

questions.zh: 「利用送快遞時有空的時間背單詞」。
questions.en: "In his spare moments."

questions.q: 关于李强，下列哪项正确？
questions.zh: 「他的收入也比以前提高了不少」。
questions.en: "His income has risen."

items.text:
这几年，一些城市开始要求居民进行垃圾分类。大家需要把垃圾分为可回收垃圾、有害垃圾、湿垃圾和干垃圾四类，分别扔进不同颜色的垃圾桶里。
刚开始的时候，很多居民都觉得麻烦，分不清楚哪些垃圾属于哪一类。为了帮助大家，很多小区安排了志愿者在垃圾桶旁边指导；有的公司还开发了手机软件，只要拍一张照片，就能知道这个垃圾应该怎么分。
经过几年的努力，垃圾分类已经变成了很多人的习惯。能回收再利用的东西比以前多了很多，需要处理的垃圾大大减少，城市环境也变得更加干净了。
专家认为，垃圾分类不只是政府的事情，更需要每个人的参与。只有大家都从身边的小事做起，才能真正保护好我们的环境。

tr.en: In recent years some cities have begun asking residents to sort their rubbish into four kinds — recyclables, hazardous, wet and dry — each into a bin of a different colour. At first many found it troublesome and couldn't tell which kind things belonged to. To help, many estates put volunteers by the bins, and some companies developed phone apps: take a photo and you learn how to sort the item. After years of effort, sorting has become a habit for many. Far more is recycled than before, much less rubbish needs disposal, and cities are cleaner. Experts say sorting isn't only the government's business but needs everyone: only when we all start with small things around us can we truly protect the environment.

questions.q: 垃圾分类刚开始的时候，很多居民：
questions.zh: 「剛開始的時候，很多居民都覺得麻煩」。
questions.en: "Many found it troublesome."

questions.q: 手机软件可以帮助人们：
questions.zh: 「只要拍一張照片，就能知道這個垃圾應該怎麼分」。
questions.en: "Learn how to sort an item."

questions.zh: 「能回收再利用的東西比以前多了很多」。
questions.en: "Far more is recycled."

options: 垃圾分类需要每个人参与
questions.zh: 「更需要每個人的參與」。
questions.en: "It needs everyone."

items.text:
狗的鼻子特别厉害。科学家研究发现，狗能闻到的味道比人多得多，有的狗鼻子的能力甚至是人的几万倍。所以，很多地方都会训练狗来帮助人们工作。
在机场，经过训练的狗可以从很多行李中找出不能带上飞机的东西；地震以后，它们能帮助人们寻找被压在下面的人；在医院里，有的狗甚至能通过闻味道，发现人身体里的一些疾病。
不过，训练一只能工作的狗并不容易，一般需要一到两年的时间。训练的人不但要有耐心，还要和狗建立感情。专家说，狗只有相信自己的主人，才会认真地完成任务。

tr.en: A dog's nose is remarkable. Scientists have found that dogs can smell far more than people; some dogs' noses are even tens of thousands of times as good as ours. So many places train dogs to help people at work. At airports, trained dogs can find things that mustn't go on a plane among lots of luggage; after an earthquake they help search for people buried underneath; in hospitals some dogs can even detect certain illnesses by smell. But training a working dog isn't easy: it usually takes one to two years. The trainer must be patient and also build a bond with the dog. Experts say a dog will only carry out its task seriously if it trusts its owner.

questions.zh: 「狗能聞到的味道比人多得多」。
questions.en: "Dogs can smell far more than people."

questions.q: 在机场，狗可以帮助人们：
options: 找出不能带上飞机的东西
照顾一个人坐飞机的孩子
questions.zh: 「可以從很多行李中找出不能帶上飛機的東西」。
questions.en: "Find things that mustn't go on a plane."

questions.zh: 「一般需要一到兩年的時間」。
questions.en: "It usually takes one to two years."

questions.zh: 整段話都在講狗的鼻子和經過訓練的狗能做的工作。
questions.en: It's about how trained dogs help people.

items.text: 现在，越来越多的年轻人喜欢在网上购物。网上购物不但方便，（　）价格也常常比商店便宜。不过，网上的商品只能看照片，买回来以后，有时会发现和照片上的（　）很大。所以，专家提醒大家，网上购物时一定要仔细阅读商品介绍，（　），这样才能减少不必要的麻烦。

tr.en: More and more young people like shopping online. It's not only convenient, but prices are often lower than in shops. However, online you can only see photos, and sometimes what arrives is very different from the picture. So experts remind everyone to read product descriptions carefully when shopping online and to look at other people's reviews too, to avoid needless trouble.

questions.zh: 「不但……而且……」：方便，而且便宜。
questions.en: 不但… 而且…: convenient, and also cheap.

questions.zh: 買回來的東西和照片上的不一樣，是「差別」很大。
questions.en: 差别 (difference) between the item and the photo.

questions.zh: 為了減少麻煩，除了看介紹，還要看看別人的評價。
questions.en: Besides the description, read other reviews.

items.text: 老张退休以后，一直想找点儿事情做。有一天，他看到小区里很多孩子放学后没人照顾，（　）就在家里开了一个免费的“作业班”。每天下午，孩子们放学后就来他家写作业，遇到不会的题，老张就耐心地给他们（　）。时间长了，孩子们的成绩都提高了不少，家长们也非常（　）。老张说，看着孩子们一天天进步，他觉得自己的退休生活比以前（　）多了。

tr.en: After retiring, Lao Zhang wanted something to do. One day he saw that many children in the estate had no one to look after them after school, so he opened a free homework class at home. Every afternoon the children came to do their homework, and when they got stuck Lao Zhang patiently explained. Over time their marks rose quite a bit, and the parents were very grateful to him. Lao Zhang says watching the children improve day by day makes his retirement far richer than before.

questions.zh: 看到孩子沒人照顧，「於是」開了作業班：前面是原因，後面是結果。
questions.en: 于是 (so): what he saw, then what he did.

questions.zh: 遇到不會的題，老張給他們「解釋」。
questions.en: He explained (解释) the hard questions.

questions.zh: 孩子們成績提高了，家長們很「感謝」老張。
questions.en: The parents were grateful.

questions.zh: 每天幫孩子，退休生活變得「豐富」了。
questions.en: Helping every day made his life richer (丰富).

items.text: 你有没有发现，有的人说话的时候喜欢看着对方的眼睛，有的人却（　）看别人？心理学家认为，这和一个人的性格、文化背景都有关系。在一些国家，说话时看着对方的眼睛表示尊重和（　）；但在另一些地方，一直看着老人或者领导的眼睛，反而会被认为不礼貌。所以，和不同国家的人交流时，（　）。

tr.en: Have you noticed that some people like to look into the other person's eyes when they talk, while others hardly dare look at anyone? Psychologists think this has to do with personality and cultural background. In some countries, eye contact while talking shows respect and sincerity; elsewhere, staring into an old person's or a boss's eyes is thought impolite. So when talking with people from other countries, it's best to learn about their culture first.

questions.zh: 和「喜歡看著對方的眼睛」相對，有的人「不太敢」看別人。
questions.en: The opposite: some hardly dare to look.

questions.zh: 和「尊重」放在一起，是好的意思：「真誠」。
questions.en: Paired with respect: sincerity.

options: 最好先了解对方的文化
questions.zh: 前面說不同文化的習慣不一樣，所以最好先了解對方的文化。
questions.en: Customs differ, so learn the other culture first.

items.text: 我三十岁才开始学游泳。（　）。小时候，我在河边差点儿出了事，从那以后就很怕水。去年，公司组织大家去海边玩儿，同事们都下水了，只有我一个人坐在旁边看。（　），我下决心一定要学会游泳。刚开始上课的时候，我连把头放进水里都不敢。教练没有着急，（　）。慢慢地，我不再那么害怕了。三个月以后，我终于能游二十五米了。（　）。这件事让我明白，（　）。

tr.en: I only began learning to swim at thirty. It's a little embarrassing to say. As a child I nearly had an accident by a river, and was afraid of water from then on. Last year my company took everyone to the seaside; my colleagues all went in, and I alone sat and watched. Watching everyone having such fun, I felt awful, and I resolved to learn to swim. In my first lessons I didn't even dare put my head under. The coach didn't hurry me but had me stand in shallow water first to get used to it. Gradually I was less afraid. Three months later I could finally swim twenty-five metres. When I reached the other side, the coach and the class all clapped for me. This taught me that as long as you're willing to start, it's never too late.

bank: 而是让我先在浅水里站着，习惯水的感觉
说起来有点儿不好意思
看着大家玩儿得那么开心，我心里很难受
游到对面的时候，教练和同学们都为我鼓掌
只要愿意开始，什么时候都不晚
所以我小时候就学会了游泳

questions.zh: 先說「三十歲才開始學」，接著說有點兒不好意思。
questions.en: Starting at thirty: a little embarrassing.

questions.zh: 同事們都下水了，只有我坐著，所以心裡很難受，後面才下決心。
questions.en: Watching the others, I felt awful — then resolved.

questions.zh: 「教練沒有著急，而是……」：沒有……而是……。
questions.en: 没有… 而是…: not hurrying, but…

questions.zh: 終於能遊二十五米了，游到對面時大家為我鼓掌。
questions.en: Reaching the other side: applause.

questions.zh: 最後說明白的道理：什麼時候開始都不晚。F 和前面「很怕水」矛盾，是多出來的。
questions.en: The lesson: never too late. F contradicts the story and is the spare.

bank: 二十分钟后，司机把钱包送到了机场。我要给他一些钱表示感谢，他却笑着说：“不用，这是我应该做的。”
上个星期五，我坐出租车去机场。因为快来不及了，下车的时候我只想着拿行李，把钱包忘在了车上。
飞机起飞的时候，我心里还一直想着这件事。我决定，以后遇到需要帮助的人，我也要像这位司机一样。
正在这时，我的手机响了。原来是那位出租车司机，他在钱包里找到了我的名片，就按照上面的号码给我打了电话。
到了机场我才发现钱包不见了。里面不但有钱，还有身份证和银行卡，没有身份证我就不能坐飞机了。我急得不知道该怎么办。

tr.en: Last Friday I took a taxi to the airport. I was nearly late, and getting out I thought only of my luggage and left my wallet in the car. Only at the airport did I notice it was gone. It held not just money but my ID card and bank cards, and without my ID I couldn't fly. I was too anxious to know what to do. Just then my phone rang: it was the taxi driver, who had found my business card in the wallet and called the number on it. Twenty minutes later he brought the wallet to the airport. I wanted to give him some money as thanks, but he smiled and said, "No need, it's what I should do." As the plane took off I was still thinking about it, and decided that from now on, when I meet someone who needs help, I'll be like that driver.

questions.zh: 故事從坐出租車去機場、把錢包忘在車上開始。
questions.en: It starts with the taxi and the forgotten wallet.

questions.zh: 「到了機場我才發現」錢包不見了，很著急。
questions.en: At the airport he notices it is gone.

questions.zh: 「正在這時」，司機打來了電話。
questions.en: "Just then" the driver calls.

questions.zh: 「二十分鐘後」，司機把錢包送來了。
questions.en: "Twenty minutes later" the wallet comes back.

questions.zh: 最後飛機起飛，「我」決定以後也幫助別人。
questions.en: Taking off, he decides to help others too.

items.text:
这些年，中国的高速铁路发展得非常快。从北京到上海，坐高铁只需要四个多小时，比以前坐普通火车节省了一半多的时间。
高铁不但速度快，而且很准时，一般不会因为天气不好而晚点。车里又干净又安静，座位也很舒服，乘客可以看书、用电脑工作，有的人还会在车上睡一觉。
对很多人来说，高铁改变了他们的生活。有些人在一个城市工作，在另一个城市生活，每天坐高铁上下班。周末的时候，人们也可以很方便地去附近的城市旅游。
当然，高铁的票价比普通火车贵一些。所以，在时间不着急的情况下，有的人还是会选择更便宜的普通火车。

tr.en: In recent years China's high-speed rail has developed very fast. From Beijing to Shanghai takes just over four hours, saving more than half the time of an ordinary train. High-speed trains are not only fast but punctual, rarely delayed by bad weather. The carriages are clean and quiet and the seats comfortable: passengers read, work on computers, and some sleep. For many people it has changed their lives: some work in one city and live in another, commuting by high-speed train every day; at weekends people can easily visit nearby cities. Of course, tickets cost more than ordinary trains, so when they're in no hurry some people still choose the cheaper ordinary train.

questions.q: 从北京到上海，坐高铁要多长时间？
questions.zh: 「坐高鐵只需要四個多小時」。
questions.en: "Just over four hours."

questions.q: 关于高铁，下列哪项正确？
questions.zh: 「一般不會因為天氣不好而晚點」。
questions.en: "Rarely delayed."

options: 高铁改变了人们的生活
questions.zh: 「對很多人來說，高鐵改變了他們的生活」。
questions.en: "It has changed people's lives."

questions.q: 有的人选择普通火车，是因为：
questions.zh: 「有的人還是會選擇更便宜的普通火車」。
questions.en: "It's cheaper."

items.text:
几年前，城市的街道上出现了一种新的自行车——共享单车。人们只要用手机打开软件点一下，就可以把车骑走；到了目的地以后，把车停在路边就行，按时间付钱，非常方便。
共享单车一出现就受到了大家的欢迎。很多人坐地铁到站以后，再骑车去公司，解决了“最后一公里”的问题。骑车不但方便，还能锻炼身体，也减少了空气污染。
但是，问题也很快出现了。有的人骑完车随便乱放，把路边都占满了；有的车坏了也没人修。后来，政府和公司一起想办法，规定了停车的地方，还安排了专门的人管理，情况才慢慢好了起来。

tr.en: A few years ago a new kind of bicycle appeared on city streets: shared bikes. You tap in an app on your phone and ride off; at your destination you just park it by the road and pay by time — very convenient. Shared bikes were popular from the start. Many people get off the metro and ride on to the office, solving the problem of the "last kilometre". Cycling is convenient, good exercise, and cuts air pollution. But problems soon appeared: some riders left bikes anywhere, filling the roadsides, and broken bikes went unrepaired. Later the government and the companies worked out rules on where to park and put people in charge of managing them, and things slowly improved.

questions.zh: 「只要用手機打開軟件點一下，就可以把車騎走」。
questions.en: "Use the app on your phone."

questions.q: 这段话中的“最后一公里”指的是：
questions.zh: 「坐地鐵到站以後，再騎車去公司」，解決的就是這段路。
questions.en: The way from the metro station to the office.

questions.q: 共享单车出现了什么问题？
questions.zh: 「有的人騎完車隨便亂放，把路邊都佔滿了」。
questions.en: "Some left bikes anywhere."

questions.q: 后来情况为什么好了起来？
questions.zh: 「規定了停車的地方，還安排了專門的人管理」。
questions.en: "Parking places were set."

items.text:
中国是茶的故乡，喝茶在中国已经有几千年的历史了。中国的茶有很多种，比如绿茶、红茶、白茶等等。不同地方的人喜欢喝的茶也不太一样，南方人比较喜欢绿茶，而北方人更喜欢花茶。
喝茶不仅是一种生活习惯，也是对客人的一种礼貌。家里来了客人，主人一般会先给客人倒一杯茶。倒茶的时候，茶不能倒得太满，七八分满就可以了，因为倒得太满，客人不好拿杯子。
现在，年轻人的生活越来越忙，很多人更喜欢喝咖啡或者各种饮料。不过，也有越来越多的年轻人开始对传统的茶文化感兴趣，周末约朋友去茶馆坐坐，变成了一种新的流行。

tr.en: China is the home of tea, drunk there for thousands of years. There are many kinds — green, black, white and so on — and tastes differ by region: southerners prefer green tea, northerners flower tea. Tea is not only a habit of daily life but a courtesy to guests: when someone visits, the host usually pours them a cup first. The cup shouldn't be filled too full — seventy or eighty per cent is enough — because a full cup is hard for the guest to pick up. Today young people are ever busier and many prefer coffee or other drinks; but more and more young people are taking an interest in traditional tea culture, and meeting friends at a teahouse at the weekend has become a new fashion.

questions.q: 根据第一段，北方人更喜欢喝：
questions.zh: 「北方人更喜歡花茶」。
questions.en: "Northerners prefer flower tea."

questions.q: 给客人倒茶时，为什么不能倒得太满？
questions.zh: 「倒得太滿，客人不好拿杯子」。
questions.en: "It is hard to pick up."

questions.q: 关于现在的年轻人，可以知道：
options: 有的人开始对茶文化感兴趣
questions.zh: 「也有越來越多的年輕人開始對傳統的茶文化感興趣」。
questions.en: "More are interested in tea culture."

questions.zh: 整段話講中國人喝茶的歷史、習慣和現在的變化。
questions.en: It is about the Chinese and tea.

items.text:
小林大学毕业后去一家公司面试。面试快结束的时候，经理问她：“你有什么问题要问我们吗？”小林想了想，问：“如果我能进公司，第一年最需要学习的是什么？”
经理听了很高兴。后来他告诉小林，很多人在这个时候都会问工资和假期，这些问题虽然也很正常，但小林的问题让他看到了她对工作的热情和积极的态度。
最后，小林顺利地得到了这份工作。她说，面试不只是回答问题，也是一个了解公司、表现自己的机会。

tr.en: After graduating, Xiao Lin went for an interview at a company. Near the end the manager asked, "Do you have any questions for us?" She thought and asked, "If I join, what will I most need to learn in the first year?" The manager was pleased. He later told her that at that moment most people ask about pay and holidays — normal questions — but hers showed him her enthusiasm for the work and her positive attitude. She got the job without trouble. She says an interview isn't only answering questions but also a chance to learn about the company and show yourself.

questions.q: 面试快结束时，经理问小林什么？
questions.zh: 「你有什麼問題要問我們嗎？」
questions.en: "Any questions for us?"

options: 看到了小林积极的态度
questions.zh: 「讓他看到了她對工作的熱情和積極的態度」。
questions.en: "He saw her positive attitude."

questions.zh: 「也是一個瞭解公司、表現自己的機會」。
questions.en: "A chance to show yourself."

items.text: 很多人睡觉前都有玩手机的习惯，觉得这样可以放松一下。可是研究发现，睡前看手机（　）会影响睡眠。手机发出的光会让大脑以为还是白天，人就很难（　）。专家建议，睡前一个小时最好把手机放到一边，（　），这样更容易睡个好觉。

tr.en: Many people use their phones before bed, thinking it helps them relax. But research has found that looking at a phone before sleep actually harms sleep: the light from the phone makes the brain think it's still daytime, so it's hard to fall asleep. Experts suggest putting the phone aside an hour before bed and reading or listening to music instead, which makes a good night's sleep easier.

questions.zh: 人們以為能放鬆，結果「反而」影響睡眠：和想的相反。
questions.en: 反而: the opposite of what people expect.

questions.zh: 大腦以為是白天，人就很難「睡著」。
questions.en: Hard to fall asleep (睡着).

questions.zh: 為了更容易睡個好覺，放下手機後做些安靜的事。
questions.en: Something calm instead, to sleep better.

items.text: 在我家附近有一家很小的书店，已经开了快二十年了。书店的老板是一位五十多岁的阿姨，她对每一本书都非常（　），客人想找什么书，她马上就能找到。这几年，网上买书越来越方便，很多书店都（　）了。可是这家小书店不但没有关门，客人还越来越多。原来，阿姨每个周末都在店里（　）读书活动，请大家一起读书、聊天。她说：“书店卖的不只是书，（　）。”

tr.en: Near my home there is a tiny bookshop that has been open for almost twenty years. The owner, a woman in her fifties, knows every book well: whatever a customer wants, she finds it at once. In recent years buying books online has become ever easier and many bookshops have closed. Yet this little shop not only stayed open but has more and more customers. It turns out that every weekend she holds a reading event in the shop, inviting everyone to read and chat together. She says, "A bookshop sells more than books; it's also a place where people can talk."

questions.zh: 客人要什麼書她馬上就能找到，說明她對書很「熟悉」。
questions.en: She finds any book at once: she knows them well.

questions.zh: 網上買書方便了，很多書店「關門」了；後面「不但沒有關門」也說明了這一點。
questions.en: Many shops closed — compare 不但没有关门.

questions.zh: 「舉辦」讀書活動。
questions.en: To hold (举办) an event.

options: 还是一个让人们交流的地方
questions.zh: 前面說大家一起讀書、聊天，所以書店也是交流的地方。
questions.en: Reading and chatting together: a place to talk.

items.text: 运动对健康有很多好处，但运动也要注意方法。有的人平时很少运动，周末却一下子跑十几公里，结果第二天全身疼，（　）还受了伤。专家说，运动应该（　），慢慢增加运动量。另外，运动前要先做一些准备活动，运动后也不要马上（　），这样运动才能真正对身体有好处。

tr.en: Exercise has many health benefits, but you need the right method. Some people hardly exercise all week and then run a dozen kilometres at the weekend; the next day they ache all over, and some even get injured. Experts say you should take it step by step, increasing the amount slowly. Also, warm up before exercising and don't take a shower straight afterwards; only then does exercise truly do your body good.

questions.zh: 全身疼，「甚至」還受了傷：更嚴重的情況。
questions.en: 甚至: an even worse result.

questions.zh: 後面說「慢慢增加運動量」，就是一步一步來。
questions.en: "Increase slowly": step by step.

questions.zh: 「不要馬上……」後面應該是不好的做法，只有馬上洗澡是。
questions.en: Only a shower straight away is something not to do.

items.text: 奶奶今年七十五岁了，以前她只会用手机打电话。（　）。看到我们都在用手机聊天、买东西，她也想学。我就每天晚上教她一点儿。（　），常常今天学会了，明天又忘了。但奶奶一点儿也不着急，（　）。一个月以后，她不但学会了在手机上和我们见面聊天，还学会了在网上买菜。现在，（　）。奶奶说：“（　），只要愿意学，就能学会新东西。”

tr.en: Grandma is seventy-five and used to use her phone only for calls. But last year her thinking changed. Seeing us all chatting and shopping on our phones, she wanted to learn too, so I taught her a little every evening. At first she learnt slowly, often forgetting the next day what she'd learnt the day before. But she wasn't in the least worried: she wrote down every step in a notebook and took it out when she forgot. A month later she could not only video-chat with us on her phone but also buy groceries online. Now she sends us photos online every day. Grandma says, "Being old doesn't matter; as long as you're willing to learn, you can learn new things."

bank: 她把每一步都写在本子上，忘了就拿出来看
不过，去年她的想法改变了
刚开始，奶奶学得很慢
她每天都会在网上给我们发照片
年纪大了没关系
所以她从来不愿意学新东西

questions.zh: 前面說「以前只會打電話」，「不過」後面說想法變了，接著就想學。
questions.en: Only calls before — but last year that changed.

questions.zh: 開始學的時候學得慢，所以「今天學會了，明天又忘了」。
questions.en: Slow at first: learnt today, forgotten tomorrow.

questions.zh: 奶奶不著急，想了一個辦法：寫在本子上。
questions.en: Not worried: she writes every step down.

questions.zh: 「現在」說的是學會以後的情況：每天發照片。
questions.en: "Now": she sends photos every day.

questions.zh: 「年紀大了沒關係，只要願意學……」。F 和故事矛盾，是多出來的。
questions.en: Age doesn't matter… F contradicts the story and is the spare.

bank: 结果，鸡蛋炒得有点儿老，盐也放多了，可我还是把菜都吃完了，觉得这是我吃过的最好吃的菜。
现在我已经会做很多菜了，可是每次做西红柿炒鸡蛋，我都会想起十二岁的那个中午。
那年我十二岁。一个星期六，爸爸妈妈都要加班，家里只有我一个人。中午饿了，我决定自己做一次饭。
晚上妈妈回来，看到厨房被我弄得很乱，不但没有生气，还表扬我长大了。
我从冰箱里拿出鸡蛋和西红柿，想做一个最简单的西红柿炒鸡蛋。可是我从来没做过，只能一边想妈妈平时是怎么做的，一边慢慢试。

tr.en: I was twelve. One Saturday my parents both had to work overtime and I was home alone. At noon I was hungry and decided to cook for myself for once. I took eggs and tomatoes from the fridge to make the simplest dish, tomato and scrambled egg. But I had never made it, so I could only try slowly, remembering how Mum usually did it. The eggs came out a little overdone and I'd put in too much salt, but I still ate it all and thought it the best dish I'd ever had. When Mum came home that evening and saw the mess I had made of the kitchen, she wasn't angry at all but praised me for growing up. Now I can cook many dishes, but every time I make tomato and egg I think of that noon when I was twelve.

questions.zh: 故事從「那年我十二歲」開始：家裡只有我一個人，決定做飯。
questions.en: It starts: twelve, home alone, decides to cook.

questions.zh: 接著說做什麼、怎麼做：西紅柿炒雞蛋，一邊想一邊試。
questions.en: Then what and how: tomato and egg.

questions.zh: 「結果」菜做得不太好，可是我很喜歡。
questions.en: "The result": not perfect, but loved.

questions.zh: 「晚上媽媽回來」，表揚了我。
questions.en: "That evening" Mum comes home.

questions.zh: 「現在」回想那一天，是故事的結尾。
questions.en: "Now", looking back: the ending.

items.text:
大熊猫是中国特有的动物，主要生活在中国西南部的山里。它们长得胖胖的，身上只有黑白两种颜色，样子非常可爱，很多人都很喜欢它们。
大熊猫每天大部分时间都在吃东西和睡觉。它们最喜欢吃竹子，一只大熊猫一天要吃十几公斤竹子。因为竹子的营养不太高，所以大熊猫需要吃很多，而且很少运动，这样才能节省力气。
过去，因为人们在山里修路、建房子，大熊猫生活的地方越来越少，数量也一直在减少。后来，中国建立了很多保护大熊猫的地方，经过几十年的努力，山里大熊猫的数量慢慢增加了。

tr.en: The giant panda is found only in China, living mainly in the mountains of the south-west. Plump, black and white and very cute, it is loved by many. Pandas spend most of the day eating and sleeping. Their favourite food is bamboo, and one panda eats over ten kilos of it a day. Because bamboo is not very nutritious, pandas must eat a lot and move little to save energy. In the past, as people built roads and houses in the mountains, the pandas' habitat shrank and their numbers kept falling. Later China set up many protected areas for them, and after decades of effort the number of pandas in the mountains has slowly grown.

questions.zh: 「它們最喜歡吃竹子」。
questions.en: "Their favourite food is bamboo."

questions.q: 大熊猫为什么很少运动？
questions.zh: 「很少運動，這樣才能節省力氣」。
questions.en: "To save energy."

questions.q: 过去大熊猫的数量为什么减少了？
questions.zh: 「大熊貓生活的地方越來越少，數量也一直在減少」。
questions.en: "Their habitat shrank."

questions.q: 根据最后一段，可以知道：
questions.zh: 「山裡大熊貓的數量慢慢增加了」。
questions.en: "Their number has grown."

items.text:
这几年，越来越多的公司开始允许员工在家工作。在家工作的好处很明显：不用每天花一两个小时在路上，时间安排更自由，也能多陪陪家人。
可是，在家工作也有不少问题。有的人发现，在家里很难集中注意力，一会儿想去厨房找吃的，一会儿又被家里人打扰。还有的人觉得，每天一个人对着电脑，很少和同事见面，时间长了心情会变得不太好。
所以，很多公司现在想了一个新的办法：员工每个星期在公司工作三天，在家工作两天。这样既能节省时间，又能让大家有机会面对面地交流。

tr.en: In recent years more and more companies let staff work from home. The benefits are obvious: no hour or two on the road every day, freer use of time, and more time with family. But there are problems too. Some find it hard to concentrate at home, going to the kitchen for a snack one moment and being interrupted by family the next. Others feel that facing a computer alone every day, seldom seeing colleagues, gets them down over time. So many companies now have a new arrangement: three days a week in the office and two at home, which saves time and still gives people a chance to talk face to face.

questions.zh: 「不用每天花一兩個小時在路上」。
questions.en: "No time on the road."

questions.zh: 「在家裡很難集中注意力」。
questions.en: "Hard to concentrate."

questions.q: 很多公司现在的办法是：
options: 一部分时间在公司，一部分时间在家
questions.zh: 「每個星期在公司工作三天，在家工作兩天」。
questions.en: "Three days in the office, two at home."

options: 在家工作的好处和问题
questions.zh: 前兩段分別講好處和問題，最後一段講公司的辦法。
questions.en: Benefits and problems of working from home.

items.text:
春节是中国最重要的传统节日。不管离家多远，很多人都希望在春节前回到家里，和家人一起吃年夜饭。所以每年春节前后，火车站、机场里都是回家的人，这就是有名的“春运”。
以前，买一张回家的火车票非常难，很多人要提前好几天去火车站排队，有时候排了一整天也买不到。现在，人们可以在手机上买票，方便多了。
不过，这几年也出现了一种新的变化：有的年轻人不再回老家过年，而是把父母接到自己工作的城市来过春节，或者一家人一起去别的地方旅游。对他们来说，过年最重要的不是在哪儿，而是一家人在一起。

tr.en: The Spring Festival is China's most important traditional festival. However far from home, many people hope to get back before it to eat the New Year's Eve dinner with their family. So every year around the festival, stations and airports are full of people going home: the famous "Spring Festival travel rush". It used to be very hard to buy a train ticket home; many queued at the station for days ahead and sometimes queued a whole day without getting one. Now tickets can be bought on a phone, which is much easier. But lately there's a new change: some young people no longer go back to their home town but bring their parents to the city where they work, or the whole family travels somewhere else. For them, what matters at New Year isn't where you are but being together.

questions.zh: 「春節前後，火車站、機場裡都是回家的人，這就是有名的“春運”」。
questions.en: The rush of people going home around the festival.

options: 常常要排很长时间的队
questions.zh: 「很多人要提前好幾天去火車站排隊」。
questions.en: "People queued for days."

questions.q: 有的年轻人怎么过春节？
options: 把父母接到自己的城市
questions.zh: 「把父母接到自己工作的城市來過春節」。
questions.en: "They bring their parents to their city."

questions.q: 对这些年轻人来说，过年最重要的是：
questions.zh: 「最重要的不是在哪兒，而是一家人在一起」。
questions.en: "Being together."

items.text:
有一位年轻的画家画了一幅画，想知道别人对这幅画有什么看法。他把画放在街边，旁边写着：“如果你觉得这幅画哪里不好，请在那里画一个圆。”晚上他回去一看，整幅画上都是圆。
他很难过，去找自己的老师。老师让他再画一幅一样的画，放在同一个地方，但是这次写的是：“如果你觉得这幅画哪里画得好，请在那里画一个圆。”晚上他回去一看，画上也都是圆，那些被别人认为不好的地方，现在又有人认为很好。
老师告诉他：“不管做什么事情，都不可能让所有人满意。最重要的是相信自己。”

tr.en: A young painter made a picture and wanted to know what others thought of it. He put it by the street with a note: "If you think any part of this picture is bad, please draw a circle there." When he came back in the evening, the whole picture was covered in circles. Upset, he went to his teacher, who told him to paint the same picture again and put it in the same place, but this time the note said: "If you think any part of this picture is good, please draw a circle there." In the evening that picture too was covered in circles: the very places others had thought bad, someone now thought good. The teacher told him, "Whatever you do, you can't please everyone. What matters most is to believe in yourself."

questions.q: 第一次，人们在画上画圆表示：
questions.zh: 第一次寫的是「哪裡不好，請在那裡畫一個圓」。
questions.en: The first note asked for circles on the bad parts.

options: 有人觉得那些地方很好
questions.zh: 「那些被別人認為不好的地方，現在又有人認為很好」。
questions.en: "Someone now thought them good."

options: 不可能让所有人都满意
questions.zh: 「不管做什麼事情，都不可能讓所有人滿意」。
questions.en: "You can't please everyone."

items.text: 现在，在中国的大城市里，点外卖已经成为很多人的生活习惯。只要在手机上点几下，饭菜很快就能送到家门口。外卖虽然方便，（　）也带来了一些问题。（　），外卖的盒子大多是塑料的，用完就扔，造成了很多垃圾；另外，外卖的饭菜一般油和盐都比较多，常吃对身体不好。所以，有时间的话，（　）。

tr.en: In China's big cities, ordering takeaway has become a habit for many. A few taps on the phone and the food soon arrives at the door. But convenient as it is, takeaway brings problems too. First, most containers are plastic and thrown away after use, making a lot of rubbish; second, takeaway food usually has a lot of oil and salt, which is bad for you if eaten often. So when you have time, it's better to cook for yourself.

questions.zh: 「雖然……但是……」：方便，但是有問題。
questions.en: 虽然… 但是…: convenient, but…

questions.zh: 後面有「另外」，所以前面用「首先」，一條一條地說問題。
questions.en: Followed by 另外, so 首先 (first).

questions.zh: 前面說外賣的問題，所以結論是自己做飯更好。
questions.en: Given the problems: better to cook yourself.

items.text: 王师傅在山区送了三十年的信。他负责的几个村子都在山上，（　）还没有公路，所有的信和包裹都要靠他走路送上去。每天，他要走四十多公里的山路，（　）刮风下雨，他从来没有晚送过一次。村里的老人们都把他当成自己的家人，（　）他送信来，总要留他喝口水、吃顿饭。去年王师傅退休了，他说：“这三十年虽然很（　），但是能为大家服务，我觉得很幸福。”

tr.en: Master Wang delivered letters in the mountains for thirty years. The villages he served were all up in the hills, with no road at the time, so every letter and parcel had to be carried up on foot. Every day he walked over forty kilometres of mountain paths, and whatever the wind or rain, he was never once late. The old people in the villages treated him as family: every time he brought letters, they would make him stay for a drink of water or a meal. Last year he retired. He says, "These thirty years were hard, but I could serve everyone, and I feel very happy."

questions.zh: 說的是過去的情況：「當時」還沒有公路。
questions.en: The past situation: at the time (当时), no road.

questions.zh: 「不管颳風下雨」：在什麼天氣下都一樣。
questions.en: 不管: whatever the weather.

questions.zh: 「每次他送信來，總要……」：每次都這樣。
questions.en: 每次… 总要…: every time.

questions.zh: 每天走四十多公里山路，很「辛苦」；「雖然辛苦，但是很幸福」。
questions.en: Forty kilometres a day: hard (辛苦).

items.text: 你有没有过这样的经历：刚才还记得要做什么，走到另一个房间就忘了？其实，这是一种很正常的（　），并不说明你的记忆有问题。科学家发现，当人从一个房间走到另一个房间时，大脑会把前面的事情“放”到一边，（　）新环境里的信息。所以，如果你忘了要做什么，（　），往往就能想起来了。

tr.en: Have you ever had this happen: a moment ago you remembered what you meant to do, then walked into another room and forgot? In fact it's a perfectly normal phenomenon and doesn't mean your memory is failing. Scientists have found that when people move from one room to another, the brain "puts aside" what came before and starts paying attention to the information in the new place. So if you forget what you meant to do, going back to the room you were in will often bring it back.

questions.zh: 很多人都有的經歷，是一種正常的「現象」。
questions.en: Something everyone experiences: a phenomenon.

questions.zh: 把前面的事放到一邊，是為了「開始注意」新環境裡的信息。
questions.en: Putting the old aside to attend to the new.

questions.zh: 在新房間忘了，回到原來的房間就能想起來。
questions.en: Forgot in the new room: go back to the old one.

items.text: 我学开车，考了三次才通过。第一次考试时，（　），结果车开出去没多远就停了。第二次，我提醒自己不要紧张，可是又因为没有注意看后面的车，没能通过。连续失败了两次，（　）。教练对我说：“（　），只要你找到问题在哪儿，下次就能做好。”他陪我又练了一个星期，专门练我最容易出错的地方。第三次考试那天，我一点儿也不紧张，（　）。拿到驾照的时候，我明白了一个道理：（　）。

tr.en: I took three driving tests before I passed. The first time I was so nervous I didn't know what to do with my hands, and the car stopped not far from the start. The second time I reminded myself not to be nervous, but I failed again for not watching the cars behind. After failing twice in a row, I began to wonder whether I was cut out for driving at all. My instructor said, "Failing twice is quite normal. As long as you find where the problem is, you'll do it right next time." He practised with me for another week, concentrating on the places I most often went wrong. On the day of the third test I wasn't nervous at all, and every step went smoothly. When I got my licence, I understood something: failure isn't frightening; what's frightening is not knowing why you failed.

bank: 我太紧张了，手都不知道该放在哪儿
我开始怀疑自己是不是不适合开车
考两次没通过很正常
每一步都做得很顺利
失败并不可怕，可怕的是不知道自己为什么失败
所以我第一次就通过了

questions.zh: 「結果車開出去沒多遠就停了」，原因是太緊張。
questions.en: The car stopped: because of nerves.

questions.zh: 連續失敗兩次以後，開始懷疑自己。
questions.en: After two failures: self-doubt.

questions.zh: 教練安慰我：考兩次沒通過很正常，後面說「只要找到問題……」。
questions.en: The instructor: two failures is normal.

questions.zh: 第三次「一點兒也不緊張」，所以每一步都很順利。
questions.en: Not nervous: every step went smoothly.

questions.zh: 最後明白的道理：要知道自己為什麼失敗。F 和「考了三次才通過」矛盾，是多出來的。
questions.en: The lesson. F contradicts "three tests" and is the spare.

bank: 我马上打电话叫了救护车，又通知了她的女儿。在医院里，医生说送来得很及时，没有什么大问题。
几天以后，奶奶的女儿从外地赶回来，到我家来感谢我，还给我带了很多家乡的特产。
从那以后，我每天下班回家都会去奶奶家看一看。我觉得，邻居之间互相关心，生活才会更温暖。
我家楼下住着一位老奶奶，她一个人生活，儿女都在外地工作。
有一天晚上，我听见楼下有人在大声叫，就赶紧跑下去看。原来，奶奶在家里倒在了地上，自己站不起来了。

tr.en: An old woman lives below us. She lives alone; her children all work in other cities. One evening I heard someone shouting downstairs and hurried down to look: she had fallen at home and couldn't get up. I immediately called an ambulance and let her daughter know. At the hospital the doctor said she had been brought in in time and nothing serious was wrong. A few days later her daughter came back from out of town, visited us to thank me, and brought me lots of specialities from her home town. Since then I drop in on the old woman every day on my way home from work. I feel that only when neighbours look out for each other does life become warmer.

questions.zh: 先介紹老奶奶：一個人生活，兒女在外地。
questions.en: First, the old woman who lives alone.

questions.zh: 「有一天晚上」，奶奶倒在了地上。
questions.en: "One evening" she falls.

questions.zh: 「我馬上打電話」叫救護車，去了醫院。
questions.en: "I immediately called" an ambulance.

questions.zh: 「幾天以後」，奶奶的女兒來感謝我。
questions.en: "A few days later" her daughter thanks me.

questions.zh: 「從那以後」我每天去看奶奶，是故事的結尾。
questions.en: "Since then": the ending.

items.text:
在很多大城市，人们很难找到一块地方种花种菜。于是，有人想出了一个好办法：在楼的最上面建花园，大家叫它“空中花园”。
空中花园有很多好处。夏天的时候，楼的最上面被太阳晒得很热，种上花草以后，楼里的温度能降低好几度，可以节省不少开空调的钱。另外，花草还能让空气变得更新鲜，也给城市里的鸟提供了休息的地方。
对住在楼里的人来说，空中花园也是一个休息和交流的好地方。下班以后，邻居们会上去浇浇花、聊聊天，原来不认识的人也慢慢变成了朋友。
不过，建空中花园并不简单。楼要能放下很多土和水，还要注意下雨的时候，水不能流进楼里去。

tr.en: In many big cities it's hard to find somewhere to grow flowers and vegetables, so someone came up with a good idea: gardens on top of buildings, called “sky gardens”. Roof gardens have many benefits. In summer the sun bakes the roof; with plants on it, the temperature inside can drop by several degrees, saving quite a lot on air-conditioning. Plants also freshen the air and give the city's birds a place to rest. For the people in the building, a roof garden is a good place to relax and meet: after work, neighbours go up to water the flowers and chat, and strangers slowly become friends. But building one isn't simple: the roof must be able to hold a lot of soil and water, and you must make sure rain doesn't run down into the building.

questions.q: 人们为什么建空中花园？
options: 城市里很难找到地方种花
questions.zh: 「人們很難找到一塊地方種花種菜。於是……」。
questions.en: Hard to find room to grow things.

questions.zh: 「樓裡的溫度能降低好幾度」。
questions.en: "The temperature inside drops."

options: 空中花园让邻居变成了朋友
questions.zh: 「原來不認識的人也慢慢變成了朋友」。
questions.en: "Strangers become friends."

questions.q: 建空中花园要注意什么？
questions.zh: 「要注意下雨的時候，水不能流進樓裡去」。
questions.en: "Rain must not run into the building."

items.text:
小周在北京学了两年中文，可是一直不太敢说。后来，一位中国朋友给她介绍了一种学语言的办法——“语言交换”。
语言交换的意思是，两个说不同语言的人互相当对方的老师。比如小周想学中文，而她的中国朋友小马想学英语，她们就每个星期见两次面，前一个小时说中文，后一个小时说英语。
这种办法不用花钱，而且练习的都是生活中真正用得上的话。因为对方也在学外语，所以说错了也不会不好意思。半年以后，小周已经能用中文和别人轻松地聊天了，小马的英语也进步了很多。

tr.en: Xiao Zhou had studied Chinese in Beijing for two years but never quite dared to speak. Then a Chinese friend told her about a way of learning languages: the "language exchange". It means two people who speak different languages act as each other's teacher. Xiao Zhou wanted to learn Chinese and her friend Xiao Ma wanted to learn English, so they met twice a week, speaking Chinese for the first hour and English for the second. It costs nothing, and what they practise is language really used in daily life; and since the other person is learning a foreign language too, mistakes aren't embarrassing. Six months later Xiao Zhou could chat easily in Chinese, and Xiao Ma's English had improved a lot too.

questions.q: 刚开始，小周学中文的问题是：
questions.zh: 「可是一直不太敢說」。
questions.en: "She never dared to speak."

options: 一半时间说中文，一半时间说英语
questions.zh: 「前一個小時說中文，後一個小時說英語」。
questions.en: "An hour of each."

questions.q: 关于语言交换，下列哪项正确？
questions.zh: 「這種辦法不用花錢」。
questions.en: "It costs nothing."

options: 两个人的外语都进步了
questions.zh: 小周能輕鬆地聊天了，小馬的英語也進步了很多。
questions.en: Both improved.

items.text:
饺子是中国北方人最喜欢的食物之一。在北方，过春节的时候，很多家庭都要一起包饺子。大家一边包一边聊天，非常热闹。
饺子的种类很多，可以放肉，也可以放菜，每个家庭都有自己的做法。有的人家还会在一个饺子里放一块钱，谁吃到这个饺子，就说明他新的一年会有好运气。
现在，超市里也能买到做好的饺子，回家煮一下就能吃，非常方便。不过，很多人还是觉得，自己家里包的饺子最好吃，因为里面有家的味道。

tr.en: Dumplings are one of northern Chinese people's favourite foods. In the north, at the Spring Festival, many families make dumplings together, chatting as they wrap them — very lively. There are many kinds, with meat or vegetables, and every family has its own way. Some families hide a coin in one dumpling: whoever gets it will have good luck in the new year. Now supermarkets sell ready-made dumplings that you just boil at home, which is very convenient. Still, many people feel the dumplings made at home taste best, because they taste of home.

questions.q: 在北方，过春节的时候人们常常：
questions.zh: 「過春節的時候，很多家庭都要一起包餃子」。
questions.en: "Families make dumplings together."

questions.q: 吃到放了钱的饺子，说明：
questions.zh: 「誰吃到這個餃子，就說明他新的一年會有好運氣」。
questions.en: "Good luck in the new year."

questions.q: 关于超市里的饺子，可以知道：
questions.zh: 「回家煮一下就能吃，非常方便」。
questions.en: "Very convenient."

questions.q: 很多人觉得自己家包的饺子最好吃，是因为：
questions.zh: 「因為裡面有家的味道」。
questions.en: "They taste of home."

items.text:
刘经理每天都很忙，可是常常觉得一天下来，重要的事情一件也没做完。后来，他的一个朋友教了他一个办法：每天早上上班以后，先花五分钟，把今天要做的事情写下来，然后按照重要的程度排好顺序，先做最重要的那件。
刚开始，刘经理觉得这个办法太简单了，没什么用。可是试了一个月以后，他发现自己每天都能把最重要的工作完成，下班也比以前早了。他说：“原来忙不一定有效率，关键是要先做重要的事。”

tr.en: Manager Liu was busy every day, yet often felt that by the end of it not one important thing was finished. Then a friend taught him a method: each morning at work, spend five minutes writing down the day's tasks, put them in order of importance, and do the most important first. At first he thought it too simple to be of use. But after trying it for a month he found he finished his most important work every day and left work earlier than before. He says, "Being busy isn't the same as being efficient; the key is to do the important things first."

questions.zh: 「重要的事情一件也沒做完」。
questions.en: "Not one important thing finished."

questions.zh: 「按照重要的程度排好順序，先做最重要的那件」。
questions.en: "Do the most important first."

questions.q: 试了一个月以后，刘经理：
questions.zh: 「下班也比以前早了」。
questions.en: "He left work earlier."
